description: Interoperability vectors for Cenya sealed credentials (docs/agente-v2-nucleo.md, section 3.1). Generated by the agent's own code (agent/sealing.py). The server's WebCrypto and Python implementations must open 'envelope' with 'private_key_pem_TEST_ONLY', and envelopes they produce for 'public_key_pem' must open with the agent (agent/tests/test_sealing.py).
WARNING: TEST ONLY. This private key is public: never use it, or anything sealed with it, for real data.

aes_gcm_check.comment: The symmetric half on its own, deterministic: AES-256-GCM(key, iv, plaintext_utf8, aad) = ct (ciphertext followed by the 16-byte tag).

notes: Envelope: JSON object {"v": 1, "alg": "RSA-OAEP-256+A256GCM", "ek", "iv", "ct"}. 'v' must be the integer 1 (not true, not "1"); 'alg' must be exactly that string. Unknown extra fields are ignored.

Base64: standard alphabet (+ and /), WITH '=' padding, no whitespace, no line breaks, no URL-safe alphabet. The agent rejects anything else (length not a multiple of 4, characters outside the alphabet).
Content key K: 32 random bytes (AES-256). WebCrypto: generateKey({name: 'AES-GCM', length: 256}, true, ['encrypt']) and exportKey('raw').
iv: 12 random bytes (96 bits), fresh for every envelope. 'iv' must decode to exactly 12 bytes.

ct: AES-256-GCM ciphertext with the 16-byte (128-bit) tag APPENDED at the end, exactly as WebCrypto encrypt({name: 'AES-GCM', iv, additionalData: aad, tagLength: 128}) and Python AESGCM.encrypt return it. Not separated, not prepended.

ek: RSA-OAEP of the 32 raw bytes of K with the agent's public key, hash SHA-256, MGF1 with SHA-256, EMPTY label (no label at all; WebCrypto: {name: 'RSA-OAEP'} without 'label'; importKey('spki', ..., {name: 'RSA-OAEP', hash: 'SHA-256'})). 'ek' must decode to exactly modulus-size bytes (384 for RSA-3072).
AAD: the UTF-8 bytes of 'cenya-seal-v1|<agent uuid>|<subject id>', no trailing newline, '|' as separator (0x7C).

Agent uuid in the AAD: canonical form, lowercase hex with hyphens, 36 characters (what Django's str(UUIDField) gives). The agent canonicalises whatever it has before building the AAD; the sealer must do the same.

Subject id: for a stored credential, its 'id' exactly as sent in config.credentials[].id (opaque, not trimmed, not lowercased); for the NetBox token of a netbox_export order, the order 'id'. At most 200 characters.

Plaintext: UTF-8 JSON object with only the secret fields: {"secret": ..., "priv_secret": ...} (an SNMP v2c community goes in 'secret'). Key order and whitespace do not matter to the agent; it seals with compact separators and no ASCII escaping, like JSON.stringify. For netbox_export the plaintext is {"secret": "<token>"} and may add {"url": "<the NetBox URL>"}: if present, the agent refuses the order when the order's url differs (trailing slash ignored).

Keys: RSA, public exponent 65537, 3072 bits for agents (the agent accepts 3072 to 8192 bits when resealing for another agent and refuses anything shorter). Public key travels as PEM SubjectPublicKeyInfo ('-----BEGIN PUBLIC KEY-----').

Any failure (wrong key, wrong agent uuid, wrong subject id, flipped bit anywhere, wrong sizes) makes the agent skip that credential and count it in the collector note credentials/sealed_unreadable; it never says which check failed to the server.
